MJRS · Remittance Process Transformation6
Accuracy

Checks that catch problems before sending

  • Totals checked. Each supplier's total is recomputed from its invoice lines and compared with the total in the bank file, to the cent. A mismatch shows a warning.
  • Credits read correctly. Negative amounts that the bank file writes with a trailing minus (for example 680780.74-) are read as negative.
  • Missing details flagged. Suppliers with no valid email, or not found in the email list, are shown in red and cannot be ticked for sending.
  • Right template per country. AU and NZ letterhead, lookup columns and total wording are handled separately.
  • Preview first. Every PDF and email can be reviewed before anything is sent.
Evidence from testing
An earlier version misread one real credit line and overstated that supplier's total by about $1.43 million. The total check flagged it and it was fixed. On a real 194-supplier export the fixed version produced no mismatches and no warnings, with every total matching to the cent.
Suppliers with no email on file are flagged in red and cannot be selected. Sample data.

Reporting and visibility

A record of every run

  • Activity log saved automatically after every run, including runs that were stopped early.
  • Send history workbook (.xlsx) on request: supplier, country, email, status, sent-as, PDF file name and total.
  • Errors sheet appears only when something failed.
  • Summary sheet with sent, failed and total value sent.
  • Save all PDFs into a dated folder; suppliers with no email go into their own "send by post" folder.

MJRS · Remittance Process Transformation9
Security and audit trail

Control without storing passwords

  • No email password stored. Sending uses the user's own signed-in Outlook.
  • Data stays on the user's PC. The licence service receives only a device ID, company name and app version, never remittance data.
  • Sender made visible. Send as yourself, as a shared mailbox or on behalf of one; the From and Sender lines are previewed, and a test email to yourself checks it first.
  • Licence control. Each copy is locked to one PC, has an expiry date and can be revoked remotely; approvals and revocations are logged.
  • Activity log after every run lists what was sent and what failed.
Settings: choose how emails are sent, with a live preview of the headers Outlook will apply. Sample screen.
